intended_object: The imaginary (vector) part of a (generalized) quaternion: x ↦ x − re(x)·1, i.e. 0 + x₁i + x₂j + x₃k (from the docstring and name).
explanation: The body ⟨0, x.imI, x.imJ, x.imK⟩ keeps the i, j and k coordinates and sets the scalar coordinate to 0. That is the standard imaginary part in the coordinates QuaternionAlgebra uses. It needs only [Zero R], which is minimal. The docstring openly notes that when c₂ ≠ 0 the notion behaves less well, because the span of i, j, k is not closed under star; this is a documented caveat, not a discrepancy with the docstring. When c₂ = 0 (the classical algebras ℍ[R,a,b] and Hamilton's quaternions), it is exactly the textbook imaginary part. This definition is itself in Mathlib, so there is no other declaration to cite.
